Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has released another N5bn to settle outstanding gratuities and death benefits owed to retired civil servants and families of deceased public servants. The payment, which is the seventh tranche under the state government’s pension settlement programme, brings the total amount committed by the administration towards clearing the liabilities to N37bn. This was disclosed in a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, on Monday. Yusuf made the disclosure on Monday during the distribution of the seventh tranche at the Government House, Kano, where he reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to clearing the for inherited pension backlog. “We inherited substantial unpaid gratuities, retirement benefits and death entitlements that had accumulated over several years. Failing to pay retirees their legitimate entitlements after decades of public service is an injustice that this administration is determined to correct,” the governor said. Add us to your Preferred Sources He stated that the payments had provided financial relief to thousands of households, eased economic hardship and restored the dignity of retired public servants and families of deceased workers. “Although some beneficiaries are still awaiting their entitlements, I assure them that the state government will settle all outstanding pension liabilities by April 2027,” Yusuf said. The governor also commended retired civil servants for their patience, sacrifices and contributions to the development of the state. “Every eligible beneficiary will receive their outstanding entitlements. We will not abandon those who dedicated their lives to serving Kano State,” he added. Yusuf praised the Kano State Pension Fund Trustees, the Office of the Head of Civil Service, the Ministry of Finance and the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, led by its President, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, for their contributions to the settlement programme. He also acknowledged an award presented to him by the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria in recognition of his administration’s efforts to address pension liabilities. He appreciated the Correspondents’ Association of Nigeria for recognising him as its Friendly Governor of the Year 2026. The governor further commended the Emir of Kano, Dr Muhammadu Sanusi II, for his continued support for the welfare of senior citizens and the people of the state. Hussaini Ibrahim
